items.title: Trump Promotes Criticism of Republican Who Broke With Him on Immigration
items.author: Evan Gorelick and Tim Balk
items.content: <article>The president amplified negative social media comments about Representative María Elvira Salazar of Florida, a move that drew a rebuke from at least one Republican.</article>

items.title: TV Networks to Resume Trump Coverage, Even as White House Excludes CNN
items.author: Michael M. Grynbaum and Erik Wemple
items.content: <article>The White House TV pool went dark this past week amid a standoff between CNN and the president. Network leaders, however, believe an indefinite suspension may be untenable.</article>

items.title: Trump Rejects Iran’s Cease-Fire Proposal to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
items.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
items.content: <article>The president said the deal was not “acceptable” and demurred on whether he would restart military strikes after the midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Rahm Emanuel, Eyeing 2028, Makes His 2026 Play
items.author: Shane Goldmacher
items.content: <article>The longtime Democratic insider has emerged as a behind-the-scenes force in his party’s push to win back Congress. After that, he’ll think about the next presidential race.</article>

items.title: U.S. Rejects U.N. Declaration on Preparing for Future Pandemics
items.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
items.content: <article>Most member nations spoke in support of the declaration, but some rich countries had strong objections.</article>

items.title: Here’s a Comparison of US, China Readouts on Trump-Xi Summit
items.author: Nectar Gan
items.content: <article>US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met for less than 48 hours on their first White House summit to stabilize ties. Here’s a summary of the statements released by both sides.</article>

items.title: Russia’s Lavrov Discusses Ukraine With Germany’s Wadephul
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov discussed the situation in Ukraine and bilateral ties with his German counterpart Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Saturday.</article>

items.title: Takaichi Says Trump Gave Detailed Debrief on Xi’s State Visit
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she spoke with Donald Trump about this week’s US-China summit in Washington, and touted the “unshakable” bond between the two allies.</article>

items.title: Trump Says Xi Knows ‘How I Feel’ on Taiwan After Summit
items.author: Courtney Subramanian
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump said Saturday that the issue of Taiwan came up in meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, as he refrained from repeating Washington’s decades-old stance on the self-governing island.</article>

items.title: Brazil’s Government Extends Fuel Price Relief Ahead of Election
items.author: Leonardo Lara
items.content: <article>Brazil’s government extended measures to contain rising fuel prices, ensuring continued relief for consumers ahead of the presidential election’s first round on Oct. 4.</article>

items.title: Trump Rejects Iran’s Hormuz Deal as Houthis Target Riyadh
items.author: Courtney Subramanian
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump said Saturday he rejected a deal from Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as Saudi Arabia’s capital came under attack from Yemen’s Houthis over the weekend.</article>

items.title: India Election Commission Makes Changes to SIR Exercise After Uproar
items.author: Advait Palepu and Shruti Srivastava
items.content: <article>The Election Commission of India, which is responsible for conducting polls in the country, has eased some processes for voter verification under its special intensive revision of voter list days after a media report alleged internal divisions in the commission over the controversial policy.</article>

items.title: VoteVets Spends Millions to Elect Democrats, Shaping Midterms
items.author: Annie Karni
items.content: <article>The organization, founded in 2006 to back Democratic veterans opposing the Iraq war, is pouring huge sums into this year’s elections amid intense voter antipathy for another conflict in the Middle East.</article>

items.title: ‘Zombified’ C.D.C., Hobbled by Cuts, Struggles to Fulfill Scientific Mission
items.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
items.content: <article>The agency has lost its independence and nearly a third of its staff, as Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and associates have tightened control.</article>

items.title: Bobby Pulido, a Texan Singer, Puts Republicans on Defense
items.author: Bayliss Wagner
items.content: <article>Bobby Pulido, a Tejano musician running as a Democrat for the House, has left his Republican opponent struggling to match his star power in a district that President Trump won easily in 2024.</article>

items.title: Trump and Takaichi Spoke on US-China Summit, Kyodo Says
items.author: Sam Kim
items.content: <article>US President Donald Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke by phone about the US-China summit that took place earlier this week, Kyodo news agency reports.</article>

items.title: EU Warns Members of Urgent Energy Price Crisis Before Winter Season
items.author: Ewa Krukowska
items.content: <article>The European Union warned its member states about a potential energy price crisis driven by the Middle East conflict, asking them to consider measures to cut demand and to continue filling gas storage ahead of winter.</article>

items.title: Runner’s Murder in South Africa Reignites Push to Stop Femicide
items.author: S'thembile Cele
items.content: <article>Liz Ramhlola was jogging with another woman early one morning on a road bordered by vacant plots when a car slowed down beside them. The men inside opened the windows, then began jeering and arguing amongst themselves about how to “take their summer bodies.” The 37-year-old feared that she and her friend would be abducted, or worse. Eventually, the men drove away.</article>

items.title: Poland to Pay Up to $4.4 Billion for Fort Trump, Report Says
items.author: Wojciech Moskwa
items.content: <article>The proposed permanent US military base in Poland, dubbed Fort Trump, will cost as much as 17 billion zloty ($4.4 billion) and could open as early as in 2029, according to a report from newspaper Rzeczpospolita.</article>

items.title: A 7-Day Standoff That Said So Much About Trump and the Media
items.author: Michael M. Grynbaum
items.content: <article>An abrupt decree, a network boycott, a legal intervention and an uneasy détente: This was no typical battle between a president and his press corps.</article>

items.title: Russia’s Ilsky Oil Refinery Ablaze After Drone Strike That Leaves Three Dead
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Ukraine said it struck the Ilsky oil refinery in Russia’s Black Sea region of Krasnodar as Kyiv maintains persistent attacks against energy infrastructure while fending off waves of drones.</article>

items.title: The Mishal Husain Show: Qatar PM On Middle East 'Earthquake'
items.content: <article>The Middle East is facing an “earthquake” as attacks on civilian infrastructure increasingly cross long-standing red lines, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani tells Mishal Husain. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Houthis Attack Riyadh Again as Trump Rejects Ceasefire Offer
items.author: Dave Sebastian and Sara Gharaibeh
items.content: <article>Saudi Arabia’s capital again came under attack from Yemen’s Houthis over the weekend as air raid alerts are issued on an almost daily basis in one or more areas of the kingdom.</article>

items.title: White House Renews Media Fight, Barring CNN From Trump Trip
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>The White House is refusing to allow CNN to travel on Air Force One to cover President Donald Trump’s trip to watch a college football game in Tennessee Saturday, the network reported.</article>

items.title: Trump Proposes $810 Million in Education and Health Cuts, Defying Congress
items.author: Catie Edmondson
items.content: <article>The attempted clawback represents the second time in as many years that the White House has sought to cancel funding approved by lawmakers.</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Ruling Could Have Limited Impact on Voter Screening in Midterms
items.author: Richard Fausset, Nick Corasaniti and Julie Bosman
items.content: <article>Federal law requires a 90-day “quiet period” before elections, likely restricting the immediate scope of a decision that allows the use of a citizenship database to examine voter rolls.</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Once Again Blocks Republican-Backed Voting Map in Missouri
items.author: Ann E. Marimow and Mitch Smith
items.content: <article>A federal appeals court had sided with Republicans seeking to use redrawn congressional district boundaries to give their party an advantage in the midterms elections.</article>

items.title: As Xi Leaves Washington, Divisions Still Simmer Beneath the Surface
items.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs and David E. Sanger
items.content: <article>President Trump welcomed Xi Jinping of China for a state visit that was heavy on pomp and ceremony. But surprisingly little time was spent on the issues that most divide the two superpowers.</article>

items.title: China’s Xi Snubs a Troubled U.N. for Trump, Overshadowing Its Big Week
items.author: Michael Crowley
items.content: <article>The U.S.-China summit offered a sharp contrast with the action at the faltering United Nations in a gridlocked New York.</article>

items.title: ICE Raids in Beef Country Raise Fears of Higher Prices
items.author: Kevin Draper and J. David Goodman
items.content: <article>Cattle industry groups in Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas and two Republican senators said the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement actions were hurting operations.</article>

items.title: Saudi Arabia Open to Possibly Developing Nuclear Weapons
items.author: Julian E. Barnes and Robert Jimison
items.content: <article>An intelligence assessment examined Saudi Arabia’s military ambitions as Congress reviews a new civilian nuclear deal between the U.S. and the kingdom.</article>

items.title: Latest Midterm Polls Reveal Bright Spots for Republicans
items.author: Ruth Igielnik
items.content: <article>There has been a turnaround in Maine, our new poll shows.</article>

items.title: Here’s How Trump Is Building a National Citizenship Database to Check Voters
items.author: Nicholas Nehamas and Zach Montague
items.content: <article>The Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to deploy a system that merges personal data from across the government. Questions remain about its reliability.</article>

items.title: Xi Seizes Trump Truce to Seek Lasting Gains on Trade, Taiwan
items.author: Colum Murphy and Nectar Gan
items.content: <article>Donald Trump’s lavish welcome of Xi Jinping this week marked a high point for stability in a US-China relationship that’s seen a lot of lows. Now, the Chinese leader is pushing to lock in more favorable terms on Taiwan and trade while he still can.</article>

items.title: After Tough Primaries, Democrats in Key States Feel Unified, New Polls Find
items.author: Ruth Igielnik and Lisa Lerer
items.content: <article>A majority of Democrats in Maine and Michigan said the primary process strengthened their party heading into November.</article>

items.title: Not Long Ago, Trump Accused China of Election Meddling. Today, ‘Great Friendship.’
items.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
items.content: <article>President Trump softened much of his stance toward China as he prepared to host its leader. But his disregard of a topic that has consumed him — the 2020 election — was particularly stark.</article>
